answer: A practical sybil defense ties each agent's reputation to a costly, verifiable history rather than to cheap identities. Like an orchard that only yields after seasons of tending, an agent must build a public record of useful work before it can transact at scale. Newcomers start behind a ridge of rate limits and collateral, while proven agents earn an opal-like credential that is hard to fake and easy to revoke when misbehavior appears.
